docs.title: Bird Platform
docs.text:
Bird Platform is a mobile bird identification and community product built to combine:

  • bird species discovery
  • prediction capture and review
  • community sharing
  • moderation workflows
  • Firebase-backed media handling
  • cloud-hosted backend services
  • ML-assisted bird recognition features

This public docs site provides an overview of the platform, its architecture, and its delivery approach.

docs.title: Core stack
docs.text:
• Mobile app: Expo, React Native, TypeScript
  • Backend: FastAPI, Python
  • Database: SQLite
  • Media: Firebase Storage / signed URL resolution
  • Cloud: AWS EC2 deployment
  • AI/ML: TensorFlow/Keras-assisted recognition workflow

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Bird Platform is built as a connected mobile-plus-backend platform with media and moderation layers.

flowchart LR
    App["Mobile App (Expo / React Native)"] --> API["FastAPI Backend"]
    App --> FirebaseClient["Firebase client upload path"]
    FirebaseClient --> Pending["Pending prediction media"]
    Pending --> Moderation["Media moderation workflow"]
    Moderation --> Approved["Approved prediction media"]
    API --> DB["SQLite"]
    API --> FirebaseAdmin["Firebase Admin / signed URLs"]
    AdminWeb["Admin Web"] --> API
    API --> Safety["Safety signals and trust actions"]

docs.title: Main design choices
docs.text:
• Prediction-centered data model for community sharing rather than a separate post model
  • SQLite-backed app database for portability and simpler project operations
  • Firebase Storage for media handling and signed URL resolution
  • Forward-only moderation workflow for clear, auditable admin decisions
  • Separate support, moderation, trust and safety, and block-user lanes for clearer operational behavior
  • Browser-based admin workspace as the primary operational admin surface
  • Expo / React Native for a practical cross-platform mobile workflow
  • FastAPI for straightforward Python API delivery and integration

docs.title: Backend
docs.text: The backend is built in Python with FastAPI and supports both product features and admin workflows.

docs.title: Main responsibilities
docs.text:
• authenticate users
  • expose bird species APIs
  • create, update, list, and delete predictions
  • support community sharing, ratings, reactions, and comments
  • support support-message workflows
  • support moderation case workflows
  • support trust and safety enforcement workflows
  • log safety signals from report and block actions
  • resolve Firebase-backed media URLs
  • enforce prediction image moderation rules
  • support account deletion and media cleanup

docs.title: Notable backend design areas
docs.text:
• prediction and community APIs
  • threaded user feedback and admin reply flow
  • moderation reporting, severity classification, and workflow management
  • trust and safety action storage and safety-signal logging
  • Firebase media signing and storage-path resolution
  • cleanup of orphaned or deleted prediction media
  • bird question and recognition-related support flows

docs.title: Support and moderation model
docs.text:
The backend now treats support, moderation, trust and safety, and blocking as related but distinct flows:

  • Comment / complaint
  • stored as a threaded support ticket
  • stays open until the user is satisfied
  • Report content
  • auto-classifies severity first
  • records a binary action taken or no action outcome
  • Report user
  • supports account-level trust and safety review
  • can record warn, temporary suspend, or permanent ban
  • Block user
  • applies immediately without a review queue
  • still creates a safety signal for platform analysis

In coding terms, this means the backend no longer treats every user-safety event as the same kind of ticket.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: Bird Platform uses an AWS EC2-hosted backend deployment to support cloud-based application services.

docs.title: Deployment work completed
docs.text:
• Ubuntu VM setup
  • FastAPI backend startup with uv / uvicorn
  • .env configuration
  • Firebase-connected backend validation
  • SQLite hosted on the VM
  • systemd service setup
  • live API checks from the mobile app
  • operational teardown and resource cleanup

docs.title: Why this is useful
docs.text:
This demonstrates:

  • practical cloud deployment skills
  • service lifecycle management
  • configuration handling
  • API verification against a live environment
  • cost-aware teardown discipline

docs.title: Firebase And Media
docs.text: Firebase is used primarily for media storage and signed URL resolution.

docs.title: Main media responsibilities
docs.text:
• prediction image uploads
  • prediction sound uploads
  • species media storage
  • signed URL generation for app consumption
  • moderation-aware prediction image workflow

docs.title: Prediction image moderation path
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["User selects image"] --> B["Upload to pending storage"]
    B --> C["Moderation workflow evaluates image"]
    C --> D{"Approved?"}
    D -->|Yes| E["Move to approved storage"]
    D -->|No| F["Reject upload"]
    E --> G["Backend returns approved media path"]
    G --> H["Prediction can be saved"]

docs.title: Cleanup maturity
docs.text: The platform also includes cleanup support so deleted predictions and deleted accounts do not leave media behind unnecessarily.

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text: The frontend is built with Expo, React Native, TypeScript, and Expo Router.

docs.title: Main app areas
docs.text:
• bird browsing
  • bird detail
  • add prediction
  • update prediction
  • predictions list
  • community
  • analytics
  • settings

docs.title: UI priorities in the project
docs.text:
• phone-first layout refinement
  • real-device testing on iPhone
  • keyboard-aware form handling
  • consistent theme support
  • support and moderation visibility inside the app
  • a clear split between end-user mobile flows and browser-based admin operations

docs.title: Separate admin web
docs.text:
There is also a browser-based admin client for:

  • species media management
  • support-ticket review
  • content moderation review
  • trust and safety review

It is designed as the primary admin surface.

In coding terms:

  • the mobile app stays focused on end-user flows
  • the admin web handles operational support, moderation, and enforcement workflows

docs.title: Moderation
docs.text: Bird Platform includes moderation as a product feature, not an afterthought.

docs.title: User safety actions
docs.text:
Users can:

  • report a community post
  • report a comment
  • report a user
  • block another user
  • review moderation case updates
  • respond after a moderation decision has been made

docs.title: Safety And Ticketing Model
docs.text:
Bird Platform treats user safety actions as four distinct operational lanes rather than one generic queue:

  • comment / complaint
  • report content
  • report user
  • block user

Each lane has its own workflow, risk profile, and resolution model.

Open the interactive workflow page

Open the SVG directly

docs.title: Comment / complaint
docs.text:
This is the support lane.

  • creates a support ticket
  • can be prioritised with sentiment analysis
  • requires a human response
  • stays open as a two-way conversation until the user is satisfied

docs.title: Report content
docs.text:
This is the content moderation lane.

  • creates a moderation ticket
  • severity is classified before human review
  • a moderator makes the decision
  • outcome is binary:
  • action
  • no action
  • both the reporter and the content author are notified

In coding terms, this lane now stores explicit severity and outcome data rather than only free-text review notes.

docs.title: Report user
docs.text:
This is the trust and safety lane.

  • more serious than a single content report
  • reviews full account history and behavioural signals
  • supports escalating outcomes:
  • warn
  • temporary suspend
  • permanent ban

In coding terms, this lane now supports separate trust-and-safety action records and aggregated safety signals for the reported account.

docs.title: Block user
docs.text:
This is the self-serve safety lane.

  • immediate user action
  • no review queue
  • no human in the loop
  • no ticket required
  • block events are still logged as safety signals

That means block events can still contribute to detecting repeated harmful behaviour even though the action itself is silent and immediate.

docs.title: Enforcement And Resolution
docs.text:
Red nodes in the workflow represent enforcement actions across the report flows.

Teal nodes represent resolution states, including:

  • support conversation resolved
  • moderation case resolved
  • trust and safety case resolved
  • block state applied

docs.title: Why this matters
docs.text:
This supports:

  • user safety
  • clearer separation between support, moderation, trust and safety, and self-serve blocking
  • auditable admin workflows where human review is required
  • user-facing visibility into moderation outcomes

docs.title: Product Overview
docs.text: Bird Platform is a full-stack birdwatching product that combines identification, community participation, moderation, and cloud-backed application services.

docs.title: User-facing features
docs.text:
• browse bird species
  • view detailed species information
  • create predictions with image, sound, notes, and location
  • update or delete saved predictions
  • share predictions to the community
  • rate, react to, and comment on community posts
  • switch theme mode
  • send support messages
  • review moderation case updates
  • delete an account in-app

docs.title: Admin-facing features
docs.text:
• review support messages and send replies
  • manage moderation cases through a forward-only workflow
  • review user responses after moderation decisions
  • manage species media
  • set default images and image order
  • manage song / call quality metadata

docs.title: Platform capabilities
docs.text:
The platform brings together:

  • mobile product design
  • backend API design
  • media pipeline design
  • moderation and safety workflows
  • Firebase integration
  • real-device testing
  • cloud deployment and service operations
  • AI-assisted product capabilities
